A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey, and their main text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. V1's appendix discussions are retained as A.3 and A.7 in v2, alongside new material.

before.justification: V1 surveys existing research. Its tables describe benchmarks, its examples are illustrative, and Section 5 attributes findings to prior studies; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: V2 remains a literature survey. Appendix A.8 explicitly summarizes prior experiences and studies, while A.9 attributes empirical support to existing work. Benchmark sample counts document dataset properties rather than original experimental outcomes.

M1.justification: The three method families and the sandbox evaluation procedure remain unchanged. Renaming test-time scaling to test-time exploration, clarifying category boundaries, and suggesting future approaches do not establish changes to a proposed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets actually used in author-conducted training or evaluation. Table 1 retains its benchmark task coverage; newly discussed examples such as CodeARC are literature coverage, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods against a proposed model. Additional methods discussed in the expanded literature review are not experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 revises documented benchmark test sizes, including SCAN from 7,700 to 4,000, PROGES from 10,000 to 270,000, and CodeSeq from 1,500 to 200. These are reported benchmark-setting revisions, not evidence of rerun experiments. The sandbox procedure and observation coverage metric remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Failure Analysis appendix provides a narrative synthesis rather than tested cases, ablations, or robustness measurements. Distributional perturbations and verification loops in A.10 are recommendations for future work, not additional analyses conducted here.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable statistical estimation procedures. V2's discussion of uncertainty awareness is conceptual.

E6.justification: V2 adds qualitative findings attributed to other studies, including improved programming-by-example performance after in-distribution fine-tuning in A.10.1 and benefits of observation-level supervision in A.9.2. These are newly summarized literature findings, not new author-produced performance results. The illustrative OC value of 0.6 is unchanged.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised. The new distinctions between inductive reasoning and inductive bias are conceptual explanations; the existing verbal definition of observation coverage is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claimed first comprehensive survey, three-part taxonomy, benchmark overview, sandbox evaluation, and analysis of inductive ability. Terminology changes and additional supporting discussion do not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantial discussion of reasoning versus inductive bias, historical scope, method boundaries and tradeoffs, failure modes, evaluation advantages, and future applications. It also qualifies the RLHF–IRL relationship and recasts the exclusion of extensive ICL literature as a scope decision rather than placing ICL outside inductive reasoning.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 documents search venues, the 2015–2025 search range, keywords, selection stages, and inclusion/exclusion criteria, and links a broader paper collection. A.7 newly explains that benchmark counts came from papers, repositories, and dataset files through counting or estimation. This substantially expands survey provenance and reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The expanded appendices substantially broaden positioning relative to meta-learning, programming-by-example, and scientific discovery, including new discussions of Li and Ellis, Verbruggen and colleagues, and symbolic-regression research. Benchmark attribution also changes: SCAN cites Lake and Baroni (2018), and ILP cites Evans and Grefenstette (2018), replacing their previous attributions.

P1.justification: The appendix develops from two topics into ten organized sections with extensive explanatory prose and cross-references. Existing appendix content is relocated, Enhancement becomes Methodology, and method terminology changes throughout. The main narrative receives smaller wording, affiliation, contact, and acknowledgment edits.

P2.justification: All seven figures and both tables are retained. Figure 2 labels and several captions change, Table 1 moves ILP to its first row and adjusts spacing, and Figure 7 and Table 2 relocate within the expanded appendix. The visual design remains substantially the same.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through documented paper-selection procedures and makes the survey more useful through conceptual distinctions, method tradeoffs, and qualified scope statements. These gains are tempered by unreconciled benchmark-count revisions and overbroad new assertions: A.5 calls post-training unique to the LLM era despite Section 2.1.1 describing PLM fine-tuning. The net improvement is useful but limited.
